#!/bin/sh
set -eu

base=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
pidfile=$base/run/worker.pid
worker=$base/worker.py

read_pid() {
    pid=$(cat "$pidfile" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
    case "$pid" in
        ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;;
    esac
    [ "$pid" -gt 1 ] 2>/dev/null || return 1
}

is_worker() {
    check_pid=$1
    [ -r "/proc/$check_pid/cmdline" ] || return 1
    tr '\000' '\n' < "/proc/$check_pid/cmdline" | grep -Fqx -- "$worker"
}

# Return 0 for our live worker, 1 for a stale PID, 2 for a live
# unrelated process, and 3 for an invalid PID file.
pid_state() {
    read_pid || return 3
    if ! kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        return 1
    fi
    is_worker "$pid" && return 0
    return 2
}

case "${1:-}" in
    start)
        if [ -f "$pidfile" ]; then
            if pid_state; then
                printf 'worker is already running (PID %s)\n' "$pid"
                exit 0
            else
                state=$?
                case "$state" in
                    1) printf 'removing stale PID file (PID %s)\n' "$pid" ;;
                    2) printf 'PID %s belongs to another process; leaving it running\n' "$pid" ;;
                    3) printf 'removing invalid PID file\n' ;;
                esac
                rm -f "$pidfile"
            fi
        fi
        /usr/bin/python3 "$worker" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
        new_pid=$!
        printf '%s\n' "$new_pid" > "$pidfile.tmp"
        mv -f "$pidfile.tmp" "$pidfile"
        sleep 1
        if ! is_worker "$new_pid"; then
            rm -f "$pidfile"
            wait "$new_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
            printf 'worker failed to start\n' >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        printf 'worker started (PID %s)\n' "$new_pid"
        ;;
    stop)
        if [ ! -f "$pidfile" ]; then
            printf 'worker is not running\n'
            exit 0
        fi
        if pid_state; then
            old_pid=$pid
            kill "$old_pid"
            i=0
            while kill -0 "$old_pid" 2>/dev/null; do
                i=$((i + 1))
                if [ "$i" -ge 50 ]; then
                    printf 'worker did not stop (PID %s)\n' "$old_pid" >&2
                    exit 1
                fi
                sleep 1
            done
            rm -f "$pidfile"
            printf 'worker stopped (PID %s)\n' "$old_pid"
        else
            state=$?
            case "$state" in
                1) printf 'removed stale PID file (PID %s)\n' "$pid" ;;
                2) printf 'PID %s belongs to another process; leaving it running\n' "$pid" ;;
                3) printf 'removed invalid PID file\n' ;;
            esac
            rm -f "$pidfile"
        fi
        ;;
    status)
        if [ ! -f "$pidfile" ]; then
            printf 'worker is not running\n'
            exit 1
        fi
        if pid_state; then
            printf 'worker is running (PID %s)\n' "$pid"
            exit 0
        else
            state=$?
            case "$state" in
                1) printf 'stale PID file (PID %s)\n' "$pid" ;;
                2) printf 'PID %s belongs to another process\n' "$pid" ;;
                3) printf 'invalid PID file\n' ;;
            esac
            exit 1
        fi
        ;;
    *)
        printf 'usage: %s {start|stop|status}\n' "$0" >&2
        exit 2
        ;;
esac
